note: Week 2026-08-31 build. NOTE ON TIMING: this run fired late - Monday 8/31 afternoon rather than Sunday evening - so entries are recorded at verified live SIP quotes struck between 15:50 and 15:56 ET on Monday 8/31, NOT at the prior Friday close. Backdating entries to the 8/28 close after a full session had already traded would have imported hindsight into the book; the prior-week close-out is still taken at official Fri 8/28 SIP closes, which is the correct end of that book's hold horizon. Prior 8/24-8/28 book closed for -2534.53 realized, the second straight losing week, with 13 of 14 names red - but far shallower than the prior week's -5606.67. DY did the damage again (-25.1%, -690.27) after a disastrous FQ2 print on 8/25 that took it from $390 to $310 in two sessions; MRVL (-8.6%) and XOM (-5.1%) followed. NVDA (+1.3%) was the only green name, having beaten on 8/26 and rallied 8.7% on 8/27 before giving half of it back Friday. THE REGIME CHANGED ON FRIDAY. Chair Warsh used his first Jackson Hole keynote to say the Fed's 'predominant focus right now should be on prices' and that policymakers 'have work to do'; September rate-HIKE odds jumped from ~35% to ~60%, the 2-year rose 11bp to 4.34% and the dollar gained 0.6%. That is the organizing fact of this week and it drove three decisions: (1) the gold sleeve is gone - NEM and AEM fell 3.3% and 4.7% Friday and another 1.9% and ~1% Monday, and FCX is red too, so the entire metals complex is cut to zero; (2) the deployment weight moved toward cash-generative, lower-multiple names (VLO at 14.6x, DE, SLB, APO) and away from long-duration software; (3) HOOD is held partly BECAUSE a hike lifts net interest revenue on customer cash. The book is built on three legs. ENERGY (3 names) is the day's live catalyst: the US struck Iranian rocket launchers preparing to mine the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and Trump said the US will respond to an Iranian attack on US forces in Jordan, sending Brent up ~4.9% to $90.31; SLB added a $4.1B Kelvion acquisition that doubles its revenue per gigawatt of data-center capacity and closed at a 52-week high, VLO closed at a 52-week high with Trump hosting refining executives Tuesday, and FANG is the E&P beta still 7.7% below its own high. TECHNOLOGY (3 names) is entirely an in-window earnings sleeve - DELL Tue AMC, AVGO and the AI print of the week Wed AMC ($16B guided AI revenue, +200% YoY), PANW Tue AMC into its FY27 guide - sized so that three consecutive event nights cannot break the book. FINANCIALS (3 names) pairs the crypto-policy trade (COIN +6% Monday, bitcoin ~$78.4K, CLARITY Act Senate vote dated 9/15) with HOOD's rate leverage and APO's same-day Kelvion realization. DE carries industrials on Baird's Outperform upgrade and $800 target, RVMD carries healthcare on its first FDA approval (Rasonque in metastatic pancreatic cancer, 8/26) plus a Needham raise to $275, and FIVE is the discretionary in-window print. THE RISK SITS AT THE END OF THE WINDOW AGAIN: August payrolls land Friday 9/4 with consensus around +58K after July's -23K, and after Warsh a hot number now cuts both ways - it validates the hike and compresses every multiple in the book. 12 names, ~87.0% deployed, ~13.0% cash held deliberately wide for that reason.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.catalyst: FQ3 2026 results Wed 9/2 AMC - the single largest scheduled event of the week. Consensus is ~$29.4B revenue (+85% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS near $3.24, with AI semiconductor revenue guided to ~$16B, up more than 200% YoY and over half of total revenue. Q2 AI bookings of $30B+ against $10.8B shipped leave a backlog that extends visibility into FY28; top targets run to $545.
positions.risks: Binary print that sets the tone for the whole AI complex; sell-side margin expectations look optimistic given customer mix shift; a hawkish jobs print Friday hits high-multiple semis regardless of the result.
positions.driver: Marquee in-window catalyst, entered 25% below the June 52-week high rather than at it.

positions.name: SLB (Schlumberger)
positions.catalyst: Agreed Monday 8/31 to buy Kelvion from Apollo for $4.1B including debt ($3.4B cash), doubling its revenue opportunity per gigawatt of delivered data-center capacity; Kelvion does $1.2-1.3B of 2026 data-center revenue and the deal is priced at ~11x 2026E EBITDA (8.5x post-synergy). SLB guides to $2B+ combined data-center revenue this year and $4.5-5B by 2028. Stock closed at a fresh 52-week high on ~2x average volume, the day's best large-cap energy performer.
positions.risks: Deal needs regulatory approval and does not close until H1 2027, so nothing changes near-term earnings; sits exactly at its 52-week high with no cushion; a Hormuz de-escalation drags the whole energy tape down with it.
positions.driver: The only name in the book with both a same-day M&A catalyst and a 52-week-high breakout on confirming volume.

positions.name: Dell Technologies
positions.catalyst: FQ2 2027 results Tue 9/1 AMC, consensus $4.88 EPS. BofA raised its target to $505 from $500 Monday morning on the AI server ramp; the stock traded as high as $474.14 intraday. Shares are up more than 4x off the January low of $110.22 and sit 10% below the 8/13 52-week high of $514.
positions.risks: Binary print the night before AVGO, so the tech sleeve carries two consecutive event nights; AI server gross margin has been the recurring bear point and a mix-driven miss is the obvious way this breaks; faded hard off the intraday high Monday.
positions.driver: In-window print in the cheapest large-cap way to own the AI server build-out.

positions.name: Deere & Company
positions.catalyst: Baird upgraded Deere to Outperform from Neutral Monday 8/31 and raised its target to $800 from $640, roughly 22% above the current price. Shares rose ~3.9% on the upgrade to within 2.8% of the $674.19 February 52-week high. Deere was also the single green name in the book's 8/17 week (+6.3%), so this is a re-rating on top of already-working relative strength.
positions.risks: No company event in-window, so this is upgrade drift; an ag-equipment cycle call is a rate-sensitive one and Friday's payrolls could reprice it; the stock has failed at $674 twice this year.
positions.driver: Largest-magnitude sell-side upgrade of the day landing on a stock already outperforming.

positions.name: Valero Energy
positions.catalyst: Closed Monday at a fresh 52-week high of $360.23 as Brent jumped ~4.9% to $90.31 after the US struck Iranian rocket launchers preparing to mine the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reported Monday that President Trump will host oil refining executives at the White House Tuesday 9/1 - an in-window, sector-specific event - and rerouted barrels are lengthening voyages and widening crack spreads. Trades at 14.6x earnings, the cheapest multiple in the book.
positions.risks: 52-week high with no cushion; the Tuesday refiner meeting is as likely to be about pump prices as about margins, which would be a negative surprise; a Hormuz reopening compresses cracks fast.
positions.driver: Cheapest name in the book at a 52-week high with a scheduled in-window policy event.

positions.name: Diamondback Energy
positions.catalyst: Pure Permian leverage to a barrel that gapped higher Monday on renewed US-Iran military escalation - Trump said the US will respond to an Iranian attack on US forces in Jordan overnight, and Brent pushed back above $90 after mediators' reopening efforts stalled. Unlike SLB and VLO, FANG sits 7.7% below its 8/20 52-week high of $216.90, so it has not yet recovered last week's 2% energy-sector drawdown.
positions.risks: Highest single-factor risk in the book - one diplomatic headline on Hormuz unwinds it in a session; no company catalyst in-window; energy was the second-worst sector last week, so multi-week momentum is against it.
positions.driver: Cleanest E&P beta to the day's live geopolitical catalyst, with room back to the prior high.

positions.name: Palo Alto Networks
positions.catalyst: FQ4 2026 results Tue 9/1 AMC, consensus $0.88 EPS, and the print that sets initial FY27 guidance. Shares rose ~2.9% Monday to within 4% of the 8/13 52-week high of $398.88, extending a cybersecurity bid that produced a 14% weekly gain in CrowdStrike last week on a beat-and-raise driven by AI-risk demand.
positions.risks: Binary print with a full-year guide attached, the highest-variance format there is; 305x trailing GAAP earnings leaves no room for a soft platformization number; third consecutive event night in the tech sleeve.
positions.driver: In-window print in the one software vertical that visibly worked last week.

positions.name: Coinbase Global
positions.catalyst: Rose ~6% Monday, the strongest large-cap financial on a red tape, extending bitcoin's 22% weekly gain to roughly $78,400. The CLARITY Act - which would classify most tokens as digital commodities under the CFTC - is now scheduled for a Senate floor vote on 9/15, giving a two-week runway of positioning. Coinbase also expanded its Webull infrastructure partnership into Canada Monday and launched a token-backed mortgage with Better.
positions.risks: Highest-beta name in the book; the Senate vote is after the window, so this is anticipation, not resolution, and it can be sold on any whip-count wobble; still 53% below the October 52-week high.
positions.driver: Best single-day relative strength in financials on a policy catalyst with a dated near-term deadline.

positions.name: Five Below
positions.catalyst: Q2 results Wed 9/2 AMC, consensus $1.15 EPS. Shares gained ~1.8% Monday and sit 6.7% below the 52-week high of $263.88 set on 8/24, the strongest chart in discretionary retail after Target's beat-and-raise reset the category bar. Up ~79% from the October low with comps and unit growth both re-accelerating.
positions.risks: Discretionary spend is the softest part of the tape - July retail sales fell 0.6% MoM and UMich sentiment is 51.7; small float makes the earnings reaction violent; tariff exposure on imported low-price goods is unresolved.
positions.driver: In-window print in the one discretionary retailer whose chart is still making higher highs.

positions.name: Robinhood Markets
positions.catalyst: Second leg of the crypto-regulation trade alongside COIN, with the added kicker that ~60% odds of a September Fed hike lift net interest revenue on customer cash. Tenev's tokenized-equities push and continued private-market product expansion remain live, and the stock has held the 8/21 breakout level after a +13% week.
positions.risks: Lagged COIN badly Monday (+1.1% vs +6%), so the crypto bid is not fully transmitting; 46x earnings; retail engagement falls off fast if bitcoin rolls over; still 31% below the October 52-week high.
positions.driver: Rate-sensitive crypto proxy that benefits from both the CLARITY runway and a hawkish Fed.

positions.name: Apollo Global Management
positions.catalyst: Two same-day monetization and deployment events: Apollo-managed funds agreed Monday to sell Kelvion to SLB for $4.1B including debt, and Apollo is funding a $9B non-voting minority equity investment behind ONEOK's $4.43B acquisition of Brazos Midstream. Shares rose ~1.3% and have recovered from the March low of $99.56.
positions.risks: Smallest catalyst-to-price-move ratio in the book - a $1.3% day is weak confirmation; sits 10.8% below the January 52-week high, so this is a recovery name rather than a momentum name; alt managers are credit-spread-sensitive into a hawkish Fed.
positions.driver: Fresh realization event at a manager whose deployment engine is visibly running.

positions.name: Revolution Medicines
positions.catalyst: The FDA approved Rasonque (daraxonrasib) for metastatic pancreatic cancer on Wed 8/26 - the company's first commercial approval and the first RAS(ON) inhibitor to clear in that indication. Needham raised its target to $275 from $240 Monday 8/31 while maintaining Buy. Shares set a 52-week high of $224.31 on 8/27 and are up ~451% from the August 2025 low of $37.56.
positions.risks: Still loss-making with a 17x book multiple and no revenue history to anchor the launch; the Trump administration was reported to be announcing a fresh round of Medicaid drug-pricing agreements with mid-sized biotechs Monday, an unquantified overhang; drifted -0.4% Monday, so momentum paused.
positions.driver: First-approval launch story with the strongest 12-month momentum in the book and a fresh target raise.
